text:
The potential can be written in Cartesian coordinates because  

\[
V(r,\theta)=\frac12 k r^{2}+\frac32 k r^{2}\cos^{2}\theta
            =\frac12 k (x^{2}+y^{2})+\frac32 k x^{2}
            =2k\,x^{2}+\frac12 k\,y^{2}.
\]

Hence the Hamiltonian separates into two independent harmonic oscillators:

\[
V(x)=\frac12 m\omega_x^{2}x^{2},\qquad 
V(y)=\frac12 m\omega_y^{2}y^{2},
\]

with  

\[
\frac12 m\omega_x^{2}=2k\;\Longrightarrow\;\omega_x^{2}= \frac{4k}{m}
\;\Longrightarrow\;\omega_x=2\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}},
\]

\[
\frac12 m\omega_y^{2}= \frac12 k\;\Longrightarrow\;\omega_y^{2}= \frac{k}{m}
\;\Longrightarrow\;\omega_y=   \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} .
\]

The energy eigenvalues of a one‑dimensional harmonic oscillator are  

\[
E_{n}= \hbar\omega\Bigl(n+\tfrac12\Bigr).
\]

Thus for the two‑dimensional system

\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{n_x,n_y}&= \hbar\omega_x\Bigl(n_x+\tfrac12\Bigr)
            +\hbar\omega_y\Bigl(n_y+\tfrac12\Bigr)   \\
           &= \hbar\Bigl(2\sqrt{k/m}\Bigr)\Bigl(n_x+\tfrac12\Bigr)
              +\hbar\sqrt{k/m}\Bigl(n_y+\tfrac12\Bigr) \\
           &= \hbar\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}\Bigl(2n_x+n_y+\tfrac32\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

This matches option **(D)**.

**Answer: D**
